rounds.text: Fly-Hi Maritime Travels Ltd trades at a remarkably modest P/E of just 7.53x, offering exceptional value compared to the sector benchmark P/E of 17.95x [E1, E5]. The company demonstrates elite profitability with a trailing ROE of 61.33% and ROCE of 49.75%, crushing the sector benchmarks of 5.31% and 6.7% respectively [E8, E9]. Growth has accelerated dramatically, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month compounded profit growth of 145% and sales growth of 37% [E14, E16]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow model suggests an intrinsic value of Rs 242 per share against the current market price of Rs 44.8, leaving a substantial margin of safety of 81.5% [E31, E32]. Reverse DCF calculations show that the current share price absurdly implies negative earnings growth of -5.5%, creating a massive disconnect from the firm's actual historical performance [E33]. Conceded: operating cash flow for March 2026 was negative at Rs -0.98 Cr, resulting in weak cash conversion [E22, E23].

Despite impressive headline profitability metrics, Fly-Hi Maritime Travels Ltd exhibits a stark and concerning disconnect between reported earnings and actual cash generation [E22]. Operating cash flow turned negative to Rs -0.98 Cr in Mar 2026 alongside a dismal cash conversion ratio of -0.12x, resulting in a free cash flow drain of Rs -2.03 Cr [E22, E24]. This cash burn is compounded by an expansion in working capital requirements, as debtor days stretched severely from 101 to 146 days and working capital days climbed from 42.6 to 67.9 days [E37, E38]. Furthermore, financial liabilities are mounting with borrowings increasing to Rs 12.97 Cr in Mar 2026 against Rs 10.03 Cr a year prior, while operating margins have demonstrated an inconsistent trend over the last three years [E20, E26]. The stock languishes low in its 52-week range at just 26% of capacity and offers a flat 0.00% dividend yield to shareholders [E3, E4]. Conceded: [E16].

Conceded: [E22], [E24]. While the cash burn and working capital stretch [E37, E38] warrant monitoring, they coincide directly with a deliberate capex build-up phase where Capital Work in Progress (CWIP) expanded by 43.0% to Rs 3.49 Cr [E27], laying the groundwork for future revenue expansion. The modest borrowing increase to Rs 12.97 Cr [E26] leaves the company at a manageable moderate leverage of 0.72x [E25], entirely justified by extraordinary top-line and bottom-line acceleration, including a trailing twelve-month sales growth of 37% [E14] and profit growth of 145% [E16] that drastically outpace sector medians [E45, E46]. Conceded: [E20]. Despite historical operating margin inconsistency [E20], the metric has actually expanded by 8 percentage points over three years to reach 21% in Mar 2026 [E19]. Finally, the stock trading at 26% of its 52-week range [E4] alongside a low P/E of 7.53x [E1] does not reflect fundamental weakness, but rather a severe market mispricing that ignores elite return metrics like a 61.3% ROE [E12] and 49.7% ROCE [E11].

Conceded: [E27]. The bull glosses over the severe liquidity deterioration accompanying this capex build-up, ignoring that operating cash flow plunged to negative Rs -0.98 Cr and free cash flow sank to negative Rs -2.03 Cr in Mar 2026 [E22, E24]. This extreme cash burn of -0.12x relative to reported profit [E22] directly invalidates the reliability of the headline 145% profit growth [E16], proving that earnings are not translating into actual cash collections. Furthermore, the bull's attempt to downplay working capital strains [E37, E38] fails when debtor days have ballooned from 101 to 146 days and total working capital days have worsened to 67.9 days [E37, E38]. Such a massive liquidity drain, paired with rising borrowings of Rs 12.97 Cr [E26] and an inconsistent yearly operating margin trend [E20], shows that the company is struggling to collect cash from its accelerated sales [E14]. Finally, citing a depressed stock price sitting at just 26% of its 52-week range [E4] is not evidence of a market mispricing, but rather a rational reflection of these acute working capital risks and negative cash flows.
